t: A Lake Chad empire ruled for close to eight centuries by the Sayfawa dynasty, one of the longest in world history.
Its control of the trans-Saharan route to Tripoli and its Islamic institutions tied the central Sudan to the Muslim world.
The Fulani jihad, the rise of the shehus and Rabih's 1893 conquest ended it before European powers divided the land.
dyk: As early as the thirteenth century, a hostel for students and pilgrims from Kanem was maintained in Cairo.
ev: Mai Hummay, by tradition, adopts Islam for the ruling house
Mai Dunama Dabbalemi begins a reign that expands and institutionalises the state
Driven from Kanem by the Bulala, Mai Ali Gaji founds a new capital at Ngazargamu in Bornu
Umar, son of al-Kanemi, ends the Sayfawa line and founds the dynasty of the shehus
Sudanese warlord Rabih az-Zubayr conquers Bornu and destroys Kukawa
French forces kill Rabih at Kousseri; Britain, France and Germany partition the territory
